requirement_summary: Workload: SaaS customer knowledge-base + live support assistant (hybrid retrieval + rerank)
Index scale: moderate — ~3-6M passages initially, growth to ~12M over 12 months
QPS target: high — 800-1,200 qps sustained during peak for search endpoint
Latency SLO: 95th <60ms for embedding lookup + retrieval, 99th <250ms end-to-end (including reranker)
Cost sensitivity: strong — wants detailed cost-per-query and monthly forecasting for burst vs steady
Model preferences: open models preferred, quantized where possible; cross-encoder reranker (smaller cross-enc unless latency hit), candidate recall vs rerank tradeoff configurable
Routing/fallback: need policy for fallback to cheaper model variant during heavy load and automatic degrade to cached answers
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, trace links for slow requests
Security: SSO/SAML for console, audit logs for queries, optional KMS for encryption at rest
crm_notes: Lead from product team at InkBridge — building SearchOps layer for mid-market apps.
Customer repeatedly: 'we need predictable economics at scale' — cost per query > top concern.
They run a RAG pipeline: ANN vector lookup (hnsw/pq) => candidate set 50 => cross-encoder rerank top 10. Want to push ANN recall down to 20-30ms.
Preferred deployment: hosted API. Will evaluate Dedicated only if hosted cannot meet 99th pct latency for reranker.
Indexing notes: documents are mix of markdown + HTML + attachments; need ingestion hints for chunking and canonicalization.
Data residency: primary NA customers; legal asked about EU residency for a subset of customers — flagged as potential contract clause.

POC scope agreed: ingest sample dataset (~4M docs), run steady-state 1k qps search traffic generator (mix of fresh queries + cached prefixes), measure latency & unit cost, simulate failover to cheaper model variant.
AE/Jordan: coordinate with billing to produce 3 pricing scenarios (steady, burst, enterprise commit). Priya to publish harness + runner by 2026-03-03.
